design_rationale: The study explicitly states that participants were stratified by pathology and then assigned 1:1 using a computer-based simple randomization procedure.

domain_judgments.rationale: A computer-based random sequence and stratification were reported and measured baseline characteristics appeared balanced, but concealment of allocation until enrollment/assignment was not described.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Patients were firstly stratified according to the pathological type (AEH or EEC), and then both randomly assigned (1:1) to receive metformin plus MA or MA-only treatments. A computer-based procedure of simple randomization

domain_judgments.rationale: The open-label design made patients and physicians aware of assignment, and although the authors label analyses intention-to-treat, the primary analysis excluded randomized patients without an assessment in the relevant time window, with no clear analysis strategy for those participants.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: study physicians were aware of treatment assignment.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary 16-week outcome was available for only 125 of 150 randomized patients (83.3%), with delays or cancellations linked to logistical and clinical circumstances, and the purported intention-to-treat analysis excluded those without timely hysteroscopy; no sensitivity analysis established that missingness could not bias the result.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Thus, most (125 and 136) women underwent hysteroscopies within 16 and 32 weeks of treatment and were included into intention-to-treat analyses.

domain_judgments.rationale: Complete response was measured histologically under a common assessment schedule and the pathologists assessing specimens were blinded to treatment allocation, making differential outcome ascertainment unlikely.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All the pathologists who assessed the specimens were unaware of the treatment allocations.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was registered and a primary endpoint was specified, but the text indicates that endpoint time windows were altered from planned 3- and 6-month assessments to 16 and 32 weeks, and numerous retrospective subgroup analyses were reported without evidence of a prespecified analysis plan.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: We retrospectively investigated whether the efficacy of metformin correlated with metabolic status.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is high, driven primarily by substantial missing primary-outcome data (25 of 150 randomized participants lacked a timely 16-week assessment) and exclusion of those participants from the reported analysis. Additional concerns arise from unreported allocation concealment, the open-label analysis context, changed endpoint windows, and retrospective subgroup analyses.

design_rationale: This was an explicitly randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial using a computer-generated sequence with permuted blocks of six and allocation via sealed opaque envelopes.

domain_judgments.rationale: The sequence was computer-generated by an epidemiologist without patient contact, used permuted blocks, and was concealed in opaque sealed envelopes, while reported baseline characteristics showed no important imbalances.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: An epidemiologist in the research center did the computergenerated randomization with permuted blocks of size six without any contact with patients. The allocation process was sealed in opaque envelops. They were opened at the time of allocation.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and study personnel were blinded with an identical placebo, limiting intervention-related deviations, but one participant withdrew for non-compliance and the analysis excluded all four post-randomization dropouts rather than following intention-to-treat principles.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Participants and study staffs (site investigator and trial coordinating center staff) were blinded to study treatment group assignment... Three patients were dropped out of the study because they were lost to follow-up, and one withdrew from the study due to non-compliance and chose hysterectomy. Fifty-six subjects were included in the final analysis.

domain_judgments.rationale: Primary outcome data were unavailable for 4 of 60 randomized participants (6.7%), with unequal analyzed group sizes and no sensitivity analysis or evidence demonstrating that missingness could not depend on outcome.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Three patients were dropped out of the study because they were lost to follow-up, and one withdrew from the study due to non-compliance and chose hysterectomy. Fifty-six subjects were included in the final analysis. Data were evaluated based on 29 and 27 women in the M + M group and M + P group, respectively.

domain_judgments.rationale: Histopathologic assessment of post-treatment biopsy was appropriate and performed at the same time in both groups, but the report does not explicitly state that the outcome pathologist was blinded and acknowledges the lack of systematic double histologic review.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Endometrial biopsy was performed for evaluation of treatment response in all patients three weeks after the last day of medication... Another potential limitation is the lack of systematic double histologic analysis for all of the cases.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was registered and the primary outcome was identified, but registration appears dated 2018-09-04 near the end of the January 2016–September 2018 study period, and no prespecified analysis plan is provided to exclude selective choice among analyses or histologic outcome presentations.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The study was approved by the institutional ethics committee (approval number: IR. TUMS.REC1394.1101) and registered in Iran Registry of Clinical Trial (IRCT), (registration code: IRCT20140820018866N6)... IRCT Id: IRCT20140820018866N6 (2018-09-04).

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is some concerns. Randomization and concealment were robust, but the complete-case rather than intention-to-treat analysis, 6.7% missing outcome data, unclear blinding of histopathologic assessment, and uncertainty about prospective specification of outcomes and analyses raise concerns without clear evidence of a high-risk domain.

design_rationale: The Methods explicitly state that patients were randomized into the MA-alone and metformin-plus-MA groups, although the sequence-generation method is not described.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although random allocation is explicitly reported, the sequence-generation and allocation-concealment methods are not described, and baseline comparability is reported only for age and metabolic-syndrome prevalence in a very small sample.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Patients were randomized into two groups.

domain_judgments.rationale: The randomized analysis excluded 14 of 30 initially enrolled participants, including eight who chose surgery, rather than analyzing all randomized participants in their assigned groups; the open treatment regimens also likely revealed assignment, and deviations could therefore affect the outcome.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Thirty patients were enrolled initially, and 16 patients were included in the final analysis... 14 were excluded, which consisted of eight patients who chose to undergo an operation and were remitted, three patients who were lost during follow-up, and three patients who had incomplete data.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data were unavailable or excluded for 14 of 30 enrolled participants (47%), including losses to follow-up and participants choosing surgery, and the reasons could plausibly be related to treatment response.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Of the 30 patients, 16 completed 12 weeks of therapy, and 14 were excluded, which consisted of eight patients who chose to undergo an operation and were remitted, three patients who were lost during follow-up, and three patients who had incomplete data (no blood test results available).

domain_judgments.rationale: Histologic response assessed by D&C using prespecified categories was appropriate and applied at 12 weeks, but the report does not clearly state that post-treatment pathologists were blinded to treatment assignment despite describing the study only as single-blinded.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Treatment response was assessed by histological examination of the D&C specimens obtained after 12 weeks.

domain_judgments.rationale: No protocol, trial registration, or prespecified statistical analysis plan is reported, while several response categorizations and subgroup analyses were available, leaving potential for selective reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A comparison of response rates was performed between the MA and MET groups. In addition, we compared the efficacies of the two therapies in the presence or absence of MS in patients.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is high, driven by exclusion of 14 of 30 enrolled participants from the randomized comparison and the absence of an intention-to-treat analysis, creating high risks from deviations and missing outcome data. Additional concerns arise from insufficient reporting of sequence generation/allocation concealment, assessor blinding, and prespecification.

design_rationale: The study explicitly reports random allocation using RandList software and sequentially numbered containers to assign 96 eligible patients to two intervention groups.

domain_judgments.rationale: A software-generated random sequence and sequentially numbered containers were reported, but the containers were not described as opaque or sealed, leaving allocation concealment incompletely documented.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: RandList software (version 2.1, Germany with sequentially numbered containers) was used for randomization and eligible patients were randomly allocated to the intervention groups.

domain_judgments.rationale: Patients and treating physicians knew the assigned treatment, and the analysis appears restricted to completers rather than intention-to-treat, although no treatment-related deviations or complications were reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: In this study, the patients and physician were aware of the type of treatment and the pathologist was blind to the treatment.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data were missing for 12 of 96 randomized participants (12.5%), with unequal completion between groups and exclusions including treatment changes and refusal of repeat sampling that could plausibly depend on outcome, while no sensitivity analysis addressed missingness.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Eighty-four participants (44 patients in the megestrol acetate plus metformin group and 40 patients in the megestrol acetate group) completed the study. Twelve cases were excluded from the study; 1 case was expired because of unknown cause, 4 cases changed their therapeutic approach, 5 patients had no possibility of following up and 3 cases did not accept re-sampling after the first course of treatment.

domain_judgments.rationale: Endometrial histology was assessed through post-treatment biopsy in both groups by a pathologist blinded to treatment assignment, making differential measurement unlikely.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Two weeks after treatment completion, endometrial sampling was performed and the response to treatment was evaluated by comparing the pathologic results.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although the trial was registered and outcome measures were identified, the text does not establish prospective registration or availability of a prespecified analysis plan, and multiple histologic and thickness analyses permit possible selective reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: This study was also registered at the Iranian Registry of Clinical Trials (http://www.irct.ir/, identifier: IRCT201410275283N11).

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is high, driven by substantial post-randomization missing outcome data analyzed only among completers, with reasons that could be related to outcomes and no sensitivity analysis. Additional concerns arise from incompletely documented allocation concealment, open-label treatment, and limited evidence against selective reporting.
